where: Section 3 (DAC: code back to volts), R-2R description
problem: The bit numbering is wrong. Bits run from 0 (LSB) to n−1 (MSB), so bit n−1 IS the MSB. Writing "Bit n−1 contributes half the current of the MSB" contradicts itself and will confuse a student trying to picture the ladder.
fix: "The MSB (bit n−1) contributes half the total current, the next bit down (bit n−2) contributes half of that, the next half again, and so on down to the LSB (bit 0)."

problem: The block ends with an empty "[shown output]" label. The pseudo code produces no printed output, so the reader is left looking for a result that never appears.
fix: Delete the "[shown output]" line, or replace it with the resulting variable values, e.g. "code = 310, done = 1 after the ISR runs".

problem: The lead calls the start-of-conversion a "flag", but START/SOC is a control bit the software writes, not a status flag the hardware sets. Section 2 itself later calls it a bit, so the lead is inconsistent.
fix: Write "the start-of-conversion bit and the end-of-conversion flag" in the lead.
